1Introduction

1.1Purpose and scope

This manual describes the titan-axi system: the OpenTitan Earl Grey chip in which both TL-UL crossbars are replaced by an AXI4 fabric, the UVM environment that verifies it, and the C firmware flow that runs on its Ibex core. It is the reference for engineers who write tests, debug failures or trace bus transactions.

The IPs are unmodified OpenTitan RTL. Each keeps its TL-UL register port; a protocol bridge sits immediately in front of it. Every transaction between modules — initiator to crossbar, crossbar to crossbar, crossbar to IP — is AXI4.

1.2Conventions

Hierarchy paths use two abbreviations throughout:

F = tb_top.dut.top_earlgrey.u_axi_fabric                    // titan_axi_fabric instance
P = tb_top.dut.top_earlgrey.u_axi_fabric.u_titan_axi_probe  // testbench probe bound into it

2System overview

2.1Features

  • Ibex RV32IMCB core: instruction cache with ECC, 16-region PMP, security hardening
  • Memories: 32 KiB ROM, 128 KiB main SRAM, 1 MiB flash, 4 KiB retention SRAM
  • Cryptography: AES, HMAC (SHA-2), KMAC (SHA-3), OTBN, key manager
  • Entropy: entropy source, CSRNG, two entropy distribution networks
  • Communication: 4 UART, 3 I2C, 2 SPI host, SPI device, USB device, pattern generator
  • Interconnect: two PULP axi_xbar crossbars, four axi_cdc crossings, 51 device ports
  • Protocol bridges: 3 host bridges (TL-UL→AXI), one device bridge per IP (AXI→TL-UL)
  • TL-UL bus integrity carried end to end in AXI USER signals
  • Security: OTP, life-cycle controller, alert handler, sensors
  • Always-on domain: power, reset and clock managers, pinmux (47 MIO pads), AON timer/watchdog

Table 3-4. Reachability

HostReaches

3.5Host bridge — titan_tlul2axi

Converts a TL-UL initiator into an AXI4 master. Three rules preserve TL-UL's single-channel, in-order semantics on AXI's five independent channels:

  1. Single AXI ID. All requests use ID 0. AXI orders responses only within one ID, and Ibex's tlul_adapter_host cannot reorder.
  2. No read/write mixing in flight. AR and AW are independent; a load could overtake an earlier store to the same address. A request in the other direction is held until outstanding ones complete.
  3. Integrity carried end to end. TL-UL a_user (command and data ECC, instruction type) travels in AxUSER/WUSER; the IP's d_user returns in RUSER/BUSER. For DECERR (no device, USER = 0) the bridge generates response integrity and returns all-ones data (zero for instruction fetches), so Ibex takes an access fault rather than a fatal integrity alert.

Table 3-5. titan_tlul2axi interface

Port / parameterDirection / typeDescription
MaxOutstandingparameter, 8requests in flight (≥ the host's own limit: Ibex with icache = 8)
clk_i, rst_niinclk_main, its reset
tl_i / tl_oin tl_h2d_t / out tl_d2h_tTL-UL from / to the initiator
axi_req_o / axi_rsp_iout host_req_t / in host_resp_tAXI4 master port to u_xbar_main

3.6Device bridge — titan_axi2tlul

  • Serves AR and AW one command at a time, round-robin.
  • Splits bursts (INCR, FIXED, WRAP) into one TL-UL access per beat; one B response after the last beat.
  • Passes integrity through for single-beat transactions from a TL-UL host (AxUSER.intg_vld = 1); generates it otherwise (bursts, testbench master).
  • Answers SLVERR without accessing the IP for: ATOPs, beats wider than 32 bits, reserved burst type, illegal WRAP length. Exclusive accesses complete normally with OKAY (never EXOKAY).

Table 3-6. titan_axi2tlul interface

Port / parameterDirection / typeDescription
MaxOutstandingparameter, 2TL-UL beats in flight towards the IP
clk_i, rst_niinthe IP's clock domain
axi_req_i / axi_rsp_oin dev_req_t / out dev_resp_tAXI4 slave port from the crossbar (or CDC)
tl_o / tl_iout tl_h2d_t / in tl_d2h_tTL-UL to / from the IP

4.3Decode

u_xbar_main decodes against 27 rules (peri owns two windows; rv_core_ibex.cfg owns the two pieces around the simulation window). A hit on peri passes through u_cdc_peri to u_xbar_peri, which decodes against 27 rules of its own. A miss at either crossbar returns DECERR from that crossbar; a miss inside the peri windows therefore crosses the CDC before it fails.

NOTEAll addresses come from OpenTitan's tl_main_pkg / tl_peri_pkg, referenced by name in the generated fabric. Firmware uses firmware/include/top_earlgrey.h; the testbench uses titan_addr_map_pkg. All three agree by construction.

5Boot and firmware

5.1Image flow

5.2Boot sequence

Table 5-1. crt0.S steps before main()

#StepReason
1Open the PMP: one locked all-access rule (entry 15); clear the reset rulesThe reset PMP uses MMWP: M-mode may access only what a rule allows, and the reset rules allow the first 2 KiB of ROM, MMIO 0x4000_0000–0x4201_0000 and the debug ROM — not main SRAM (stack) or the PLIC. Must execute from the first 2 KiB; rom.ld asserts it.
2Calibrate the clocks: rewrite AST REGAL; wait for sensor_ctrl STATUS.AST_INIT_DONEOscillators start uncalibrated (IO ≈ 26 MHz instead of 96). Without it all baud rates and delays are ≈ 4× off.
3Initialize main SRAM: sram_ctrl CTRL.INIT; wait for STATUS.INIT_DONEUnwritten SRAM words have invalid ECC; a read is an integrity error.
4Zero .bss, copy .data, write IN_TEST, call main(), write PASSED/FAILEDC runtime start and report to the testbench.

6.3AXI probe

// uvm/tb/titan_axi_probe.sv (generated by uvm/tb/gen_tb.py) — one block per port, e.g. dev.uart0:
axi_if if_dev_uart0 (.aclk(titan_axi_fabric.clk_fixed_i), .aresetn(titan_axi_fabric.rst_fixed_ni));
assign if_dev_uart0.awvalid = titan_axi_fabric.peri_dev_req[titan_axi_fabric.PeriDevUart0].aw_valid;
assign if_dev_uart0.awaddr  = titan_axi_fabric.peri_dev_req[titan_axi_fabric.PeriDevUart0].aw.addr;
// ... every AW / W / B / AR / R field ...
initial uvm_config_db #(virtual axi_if)::set(null, "", "axi_vif:dev.uart0", if_dev_uart0);

bind titan_axi_fabric titan_axi_probe u_titan_axi_probe ();

6.4Fabric scoreboard

  1. Device-port transactions are queued per device as they complete.
  2. When a host-port transaction completes, its address is decoded with titan_addr_map_pkg::decode().
  3. Unmapped, or not reachable from that host (reachable()): every response beat must be DECERR.
  4. Otherwise the device's queue must contain its twin: same host index (ID[5:4]), ID[3:0], address, kind and length. Size, burst, PROT, write data, strobes, read data and responses must be identical.
  5. At a chip reset, in-flight transactions are dropped. At the end of the test, a device transaction with no host twin (older than 5 µs) is an error.

Table 6-2. Checks applied in every test

CheckerDetects
axi_if assertionsVALID dropped or payload changed before the handshake; X on any VALID
axi_monitorWLAST/RLAST inconsistent with AxLEN; B or R with no outstanding request for its ID
fabric_scoreboardmisrouting, lost, duplicated or corrupted transactions; wrong DECERR behaviour
sw_status_monitorfirmware FAILED

7.3Adding a test

Table 7-4. Procedure by test kind

KindSteps
C1. firmware/tests/my_test.c · 2. tests.list: my_test fw_test my_test · 3. uvm/sim/run.sh my_test
C+UVMAs above, plus a class extending titan_base_test; its test_body() does the testbench part (env.sw.wait_sync(n), env.gpio.vif, env.uart0.text, env.clk) and calls super.test_body() to wait for PASSED.
UVMA sequence extending axi_test_seq (write32, read32, write, read, check); a test extending axi_stub_cpu_test returning it from make_seq(); tests.list entry with firmware idle.
class my_seq extends axi_test_seq;
  `uvm_object_utils(my_seq)
  function new(string name = "my_seq"); super.new(name); endfunction
  virtual task body();
    bit [31:0] d; bit [1:0] r;
    read32(32'h4004_0020, d, r);                            // gpio DIRECT_OE
    check(r == AXI_OKAY && d == 0, "DIRECT_OE not 0 after reset");
  endtask
endclass
class my_test extends axi_stub_cpu_test;
  `uvm_component_utils(my_test)
  function new(string name, uvm_component parent); super.new(name, parent); endfunction
  virtual function axi_test_seq make_seq(); return my_seq::type_id::create("my_seq"); endfunction
endclass
// tests.list:   my_test   my_test   idle

8Observing AXI transactions

8.1Methods

uvm/sim/run.sh fw_uart_tx --trace 0x4000001c      # text: AXI ports crossed, in hop order
grep TRACE uvm/sim/runs/fw_uart_tx/run.log
uvm/sim/run.sh fw_uart_tx --waves                  # waves: every signal at every hop
simvision uvm/sim/runs/fw_uart_tx/waves.shm &
NOTEEvery AXI boundary is listed twice: the design port (a struct, e.g. F.u_dev_uart0.axi_req_i.aw_valid) and the probe interface with flat AXI names on the same wires (P.if_dev_uart0.awvalid). TL-UL boundaries exist only as design ports. --trace sees AXI ports only.

8.2Boundaries

Table 8-1. Boundary definitions

#BoundaryProtocol / clockWhat changes at this boundary
1Core boundaryTL-UL → AXI, 100 MHzTL-UL becomes AXI (Get → AR, Put* → AW+W); ID 0; integrity into AxUSER/WUSER; PROT[2] = 1 for fetches
2Crossbar inputAXI, 100 MHznone — the bridge output is the crossbar slave port
3Crossbar outputAXI, 100 MHzID widened to {host index, ID}; DECERR generated here for unmapped/unreachable addresses
2′/3′xbar_peri input / outputAXI, 24 MHzafter u_cdc_peri: slower clock; ID unchanged (single slave port)
4IP boundaryAXI → TL-ULAXI becomes TL-UL; bursts split into beats; integrity passed through or generated

8.6SimVision procedure

  1. Open uvm/sim/runs/<test>/waves.shm; in the Design Browser select tb_top.dut.top_earlgrey.u_axi_fabric.u_titan_axi_probe.
  2. Send the interfaces of the path to the waveform window (e.g. if_host_rv_core_ibex_cored, if_link_main_to_peri, if_dev_uart0); keep the AW/W/B or AR/R signals.
  3. For the struct views, select the bridge instance (e.g. u_dev_uart0) and add axi_req_i, axi_rsp_o, tl_o, tl_i.
  4. Search awaddr/araddr for the address, or jump to the times printed by --trace.
# SimVision console (equivalent to steps 1-2)
waveform add -signals {
  tb_top.dut.top_earlgrey.u_axi_fabric.u_titan_axi_probe.if_host_rv_core_ibex_cored
  tb_top.dut.top_earlgrey.u_axi_fabric.u_titan_axi_probe.if_link_main_to_peri
  tb_top.dut.top_earlgrey.u_axi_fabric.u_titan_axi_probe.if_dev_uart0
  tb_top.dut.top_earlgrey.u_axi_fabric.tl_uart0_o
  tb_top.dut.top_earlgrey.u_axi_fabric.tl_uart0_i
}

X on read datafloating pad or uninitialized memory

9.2Bring-up history

Table 9-2. Issues found during bring-up (all resolved)

ObservationCauseResolution
Bridge testbench: 397 errors, all one transaction out of stepA driver task sampled gnt (high whenever idle) before its own request was drivenAll driver tasks align to their clocking block first

ADesign notes and pitfalls

Table A-1. Guidelines

GuidelineRationale
Do not edit generated files (titan_axi_fabric.sv, titan_axi_probe.sv, titan_addr_map_pkg.sv, regs/*.h, this document)The next regeneration overwrites them, and the testbench map could drift from the RTL.
Never access an IP while its clock is gatedThe device bridge waits for a TL-UL response that never comes; the bus behind it hangs.
Do not expect the CPU to execute from any memoryThe fetch port reaches only ROM, main SRAM, flash and the debug ROM.
Compare only ID[3:0] across crossbar boundariesxbar_main prepends the host index by design.
Expect bursts to end at the device bridgeTL-UL has no bursts: one request per beat at the IP.
Distinguish SLVERR from DECERRSLVERR: a device answered and refused. DECERR: no device. Different bugs.
Check pins and timing from the testbench tooFirmware timing with a wrong clock is self-consistent; only an external observer catches it.
Use titan_sync(n) instead of fixed delaysAn explicit handshake survives timing changes and is visible in the log.
Keep shared constants commented on both sides (C and UVM)Nothing links them at compile time.
Sample DUT signals through clocking blocksAvoids races; the bridge testbench's first failure was one.
Prove bridge changes in uvm/bridge_tb firstSeconds per run instead of a minute, and failures stay local.
Read the first error, not the last; reproduce with the same seedLater errors are usually fallout; a fix you cannot reproduce is unverified.
Run one simulation at a timeRuns share runs/build and the licence pool.
